$comment: Trusted receiver signer policy, read from the PR base ref only. Evidence must carry a GitHub artifact attestation produced by exactly this pinned, privileged workflow identity, triggered from exactly this source ref (gh attestation verify --signer-workflow --predicate-type --source-ref). check_signer() additionally recomputes the subject digest itself, checks the signer's own certificate sourceRepositoryDigest against approvedSignerSourceDigests, and compares the signed predicate's own definitionSha256/assessedChecks/expectedPredicate fields -- a bare verify exit code is never treated as sufficient. This authenticates that the exact CI assessment recorded by receiver-attest.yml (structural integrity + factory allowlist + capability revocation + independent execution boundary, see assess_canonical) was produced and approved by that pinned workflow AT an approved revision -- not that a local agent's execution or any particular SLSA security level is retroactively certified.
approvedSignerSourceDigestsBootstrap: Deliberately empty (fail-closed): this receiver must never trust a signer revision it has not actually reviewed, and revision trust can never be read from the evidence/predicate itself -- only from the Fulcio/sigstore certificate's own sourceRepositoryDigest field, which the signed content cannot forge. This is a pre-selected-and-reviewed allowlist, never trust-on-first-use: approval must precede that revision ever signing anything, not follow from observing what a first successful run happened to produce. CAUTION: 'land commit S, then let it run' is NOT sufficient by itself, because receiver-attest.yml is triggered off this ref's moving tip -- by the time any auto-triggered run actually executes, later unrelated commits may have advanced the tip past S, so that run would certify the NEW tip commit, not S, and sourceRepositoryDigest pins the whole reviewed source revision, not just unchanged workflow text. Bootstrap sequence (manual, explicitly authorized, NOT part of this commit), in this exact order: (1) identify and review the EXACT candidate commit S's full diff of receiver-attest.yml (and anything it transitively trusts) against the last-approved revision, if any -- this review, and the resulting approved value of S, are recorded independently (e.g. in the reviewing commit/PR description) BEFORE S is ever allowed to execute against real evidence -- this is the approval, not the later observation; (2) explicitly trigger receiver-attest.yml PINNED to run at commit S itself -- e.g. 'gh workflow run receiver-attest.yml --ref <S full SHA>' (or an equivalent explicit-ref dispatch/checkout), never a push/PR-triggered run off whatever the ref's tip happens to be at execution time, so GITHUB_SHA/the checked-out commit is guaranteed to equal S even if the ref has since moved; (3) after that pinned run completes, independently inspect its resulting attestation's verificationResult.signature.certificate.sourceRepositoryDigest and require it to equal the value of S that was approved in step (1) -- a mismatch means the trigger was not actually pinned correctly and must be fixed before proceeding, not silently accepted; (4) only after that equality is confirmed, add S to approvedSignerSourceDigests in a SEPARATE, SUBSEQUENT receiver-policy commit -- check_signer() then verifies future certificates' sourceRepositoryDigest against an allowlist that was populated strictly after, and independently of, the run it was derived from, never retroactively and never trust-on-first-use. Unrelated later commits on this ref do not invalidate attestations already signed at an approved S, and do not require re-approval. Only a NEW commit that actually changes receiver-attest.yml's trusted behavior becomes a new candidate revision S2, which must independently repeat this entire sequence (review S2, pin-execute at S2, verify the observed digest equals the approved S2, then add S2 in its own later policy commit) before anything signed by S2 is trusted; old digests may be retired once no evidence depends on them.
